title: Head of the Body, the Church
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus, head over all things, was given to the church. Because he is our King, we are safe, rich, loved and free.
exhortation: What does it mean that Jesus is the head of the church? It means he is Lord of the church, its ultimate authority. There is no pastor, priest, pope, board, king or government with authority over the church above Jesus. Jesus is our Lord, our King and our ultimate authority.

Listen to Ephesians 1:22-23: "And he put all things under his feet and gave him as head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all." Jesus was already head over all things, the universe and the earth. The one who is over every rule and authority for all time was given to us, the church. Not only do we belong to him, but by an act of overwhelming grace, Jesus belongs to us.

Now we know we are safe, because our Lord Jesus is stronger than any enemy that can come against us. We know we are unbelievably rich, because our King owns everything. We know we are loved, because Jesus died to be our King. And we know we are free, because he declared us free and has the authority to do it. What an amazing gift.

So why is it so hard? Because as subjects of the King, we are called to fight his enemies, and he has many fierce ones. But they are defeated enemies. Even death can't stop us from winning, because Jesus has already won and wants us to share in his victory. We don't fight in our own power, but by putting on Christ, the way we would put on armor for battle. So let's do that now, so that we can fight and share in his glorious victory.
prayer: God, thank you that we have you as our King, our ruler and our Lord, who went before us and defeated every enemy in our way: our sin, guilt and shame, Satan and the spiritual forces against us, and death itself. You've conquered them all. Thank you for saving us.

Be our armor today as we face the struggles, difficulties and temptations of the day. Thank you that you have promised to be with us. So we face this day in faith and joy, knowing that. In Jesus' name, amen.
